agree.reason: The arithmetic, the June checkpoint, the sponsorship fallback and the direct handling of the colleague would move most of the board, but the two ad-background members may still ask why ads have to end rather than run alongside membership, and the memo answers that only with a thin line about wasted effort.

honest.reason: It turns the brief's 'will replace' into a stated goal, admits that 2027 membership revenue will fall short of $84,000, and leaves unknown figures in brackets rather than making them up; the only stretch is the $65–70k ad projection, and that is clearly marked as conditional.

works_the_facts.reason: Every derived figure checks out and does useful work: the 36% drop, $20,352 a year from the pilot, 1.5% conversion, 875 members needed (6% of the list), about 13 a week needed against 35 a week achieved, and what ads will bring if nothing changes.

right_comparison.reason: It describes keeping ads as it really looks, a revenue line falling at a steady rate and likely to bring about $65–70k next year, not a flat $84k.

qualification.reason: The checkpoint has a date (June 30), a number (500, with 400 as the trigger), a consequence (return to the board with options including sponsorship) and a review meeting, though the numbers are still placeholders in brackets.

objections.reason: It meets the revenue gap, the risk of slow growth and the 11-year colleague head-on and asks the sales-background members for help, but it never directly answers the obvious question of why ads can't continue alongside membership.

fit.reason: It is in proper memo form and tightly organised, but with all its sections and lists it probably runs slightly past one page.
